meaning: Devices outside the data centre that connect to a cloud service; here, the computer beside each robot arm.
An agent program on each device plus a cloud service that tells that program which software to run.
The AWS service that holds the registry of devices and the message broker they connect to.
AWS IoT's record of one device.
A thing that runs the Greengrass software.
The core of the Greengrass software on the device, in two builds: the Java nucleus (at least 96 MB of RAM) and nucleus lite, written for constrained devices and documented at under 15 MB.
The unit of software Greengrass delivers: a recipe file that says how to install and start it, plus its artifacts.
The JSON or YAML file that names a component, its dependencies, its artifacts and its lifecycle commands.
A file a component fetches, named in its recipe; one component's artifacts may total at most 2 GB.
The full list of components a thing or thing group should run; it stands, so a device that reconnects later still receives it.
A named set of things, the target of a fleet deployment.
A small JSON document per thing kept in the cloud, holding desired state, reported state and their difference.
An AWS IoT remote operation sent to devices; it carries a group deployment and controls its rate, abort rule and timeout.
An AWS IoT job's instance on one device; an abort cancels only executions still QUEUED, never those IN_PROGRESS.

In a fleet, the spread of a new policy version across the arms a few at a time, at a rate that grows as arms are notified or succeed, with a rule that cancels the arms still queued once too many fail. Earlier sections use rollout for one run of a policy.
A small set of devices that takes an update before the rest of the fleet.
A Greengrass deployment that targets a smaller group of devices inside a parent deployment's group.
A job rule that cancels the queued part of a rollout once a set percentage of executions has failed, counted only after a minimum number of devices has been notified.
The Greengrass component that trades the device certificate for short-lived AWS credentials that other components use.
The AWS service whose roles say which AWS services a device's components may call.
AWS's store for container images.
A lightweight protocol in which a device publishes small messages to named topics and subscribers receive them.
A Greengrass component that queues data on the device and exports it in the background, including files to Amazon S3.
Sending one S3 object as many parts, so a dropped connection costs one part.
One recorded attempt at the task, stored as rows of joint data plus video files.

expansion: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service Hybrid Nodes
meaning: A feature that joins a machine on your premises to a cloud Kubernetes cluster as a worker node.
AWS's label for environments whose network link is unreliable.
Onboarding many devices by shipping each with a shared claim certificate that it exchanges for its own on first connection.
The commands a recipe gives the nucleus to run, such as install, and run or startup to start the software.
A hash of a file's or image's content fixed in advance; a reference by digest names exactly one set of bytes, and a mismatch fails the deployment.
The Greengrass component that pulls the container images named by docker: artifacts; Docker itself must already run on the device.
The disk area where the nucleus keeps component artifacts, 10 GB by default.
The local socket through which a component talks to the nucleus, for example to defer an update; each operation must be granted in an accessControl policy.
Publishing to a reserved $aws/rules/ topic so that an AWS IoT rule's actions run on the message without the message broker.
In AWS IoT Core, a query over incoming messages whose actions send the matches to other services, such as an S3 bucket.
An AWS IoT feature that makes the device registry and the shadows searchable, so one query can find, for example, the arms on a new policy whose reported success rate fell.
The Kubernetes plugin that gives each pod an address; on an EKS hybrid node you install and run it yourself (Cilium or Calico).
The plugin standard a Kubernetes pod network is built on; the Amazon VPC CNI used in the cloud does not work on hybrid nodes.
The private network in AWS that an EKS cluster lives in.
A laser range scanner that measures distance to surrounding surfaces.
AWS Direct Connect, a private network link to AWS; one of the ways an EKS hybrid node reaches its cluster's VPC.
